authority.scope: GTK2 private stepper state-aware repaint prototype only. No installed theme changes.

environment.palette_fixture: RC uses fixed colors to isolate state/repaint mechanics; KDE color-role behavior was not tested.

findings.r535_failure_confirmed: An instrumented R535 run shows GtkStyle draw_arrow receives GTK_STATE_ACTIVE (2) and GTK_STATE_PRELIGHT (1) for the individual stepper while the range-level cached state remains normal. R535 does not save active/prelight in its cell cache, so its later partial repaint can use stale state.
findings.per_stepper_states: R536's four hover and release captures match each focused asset; the four pressed captures match their pressed asset exactly. For this artwork focused and normal assets coincide. Pressed and normal differ in 53/225 pixels per direction.
findings.active_partial_repaint: One pixel was deliberately damaged at the outer edge of each pressed cell. After R536 repaint, every 15x15 cell matches its pressed asset at 0/225 differences.
findings.endpoint_and_disabled: Both endpoint captures use the normal asset for all directions; a globally insensitive range uses the disabled asset for all four.
findings.input: The R521 input probe under the loaded R536 module passes 8/8: internal movement, blocked endpoints and globally insensitive ranges.
findings.independent_review: A second review confirmed all pixel comparisons and input cases. Endpoint evidence is indirect: screenshots establish normal artwork and input tests establish blocking, but the trace does not pair raw GTK callback state with endpoint_stepper() results per arrow. Normal/focused/disabled PNGs are byte-identical, so semantic roles rely on the cache-state trace, not pixels alone.
findings.cache_edge_cases: The prototype has one cache cell per arrow enum, so multiple same-direction steppers can overwrite one another. A missing asset does not refresh cached state and may replay a previous state.

limits: The prototype still has no explicit invalidation when a stepper disappears or style geometry changes without a full redraw.
Only the common one-back/one-forward layout was tested; secondary steppers, resize while active, endpoint or disabled, and cache invalidation on style/palette change remain unverified.
A missing-asset fallback can leave an older cached state eligible for repaint.
PNG files are reopened during drawing; no performance or asset-cache work was tested.
The fixture does not test KDE color roles, palette reload, contrast, or other schemes.
There was no fresh VM comparison, personal application comparison, installation or user visual acceptance.
next: Review and fix cell-cache invalidation and per-style asset lifetime in a private GTK2 engine. Then validate role-derived palette outputs and real application/VM rendering without changing installed files until the focused implementation and SR10.4 comparison are sound.
